cards.name: Hand-drawn wobbly outline
cards.summary: Clean vector shapes and outlined type get slightly wobbly, hand-inked or hand-cut edges, like a marker drawing or a paper cut-out.
use_for: hand-drawn style for flat vector illustrations
a playful variant of a too-perfect geometric logo
avoid: small body text: letters lose legibility; keep it to display type and shapes
an outline that must repeat exactly: both effects are random and re-jitter when the art is edited; expand or convert to curves to freeze the result
torn-paper edges with sharp spikes: use Roughen with corner points (roundness 0) instead
cutter or plotter files: bake the effect and check the node count first

steps.note: On the whole object or group (object level) so fill and stroke wobble together; smooth points (roundness 1) give a soft hand-drawn wave. The verified render used 12 pt / detail 12 with corner points; these gentler values use the same keys.
A small Tweak after Roughen bends the existing anchors and handles so the line looks drawn, not vibrated; keep 2-5 pt.
Optional: Object > Expand Appearance freezes the random outline into real paths before hand-off.

steps.script:
for k in ("orange_box", "blue_star", "grad_circle", "pgd_type", "zigzag"):
    sh = labels[k]
    sh.CreateZipperDistortion(sh.CenterX, sh.CenterY, 4, 6, True, True, False)
result = labels["blue_star"]
steps.note: Zipper distortion on every plate shape (CreateZipperDistortion at each shape's centre, amplitude 4, frequency 6, Random and Smooth on): the edges turn into irregular soft waves.
Convert to Curves on every shape bakes the distortion into plain nodes so it no longer re-rolls.

verified.note: Every plate shape gets soft irregular wobbly edges: the box, star and circle look hand cut, the type looks hand inked and the zigzag gains a jittery line; baked to curves in step 2.

manual_steps: CorelDRAW: to roughen only part of an edge, brush it by hand with the Roughen tool (Edit Shape flyout); the tool cannot be scripted.
Illustrator: check that fill and stroke still line up after Roughen (the scripted render on a filled + stroked rectangle moved them apart); if not, apply at object level or expand first.

cards.name: Scribble / marker hatch fill
cards.summary: Solid fills are redrawn as loose back-and-forth marker strokes, so flat shapes look coloured in with a felt pen or hatched with ink.
avoid: small type: the scribble destroys legibility; scribble a shape behind the type instead
large areas with tight spacing and thin lines: thousands of segments, slow files
an even mechanical hatch: use a line pattern swatch
CorelDRAW: PGD has no vector scribble effect there; its Art Strokes (Pen & Ink, Sketch Pad) are bitmap effects that need the art converted to a bitmap first

steps.note: On a fill-only appearance (or an extra fill above a clean outline) so the outline stays crisp; StrokeWidth and Spacing in pt, Spacing about twice StrokeWidth for visible gaps. Verified at Spacing 10, StrokeWidth 4, Angle 45.
Optional: freeze the random scribble before export (expect a heavy path count).

manual_steps: Quick alternative: apply the 'Scribble 6' graphic style (bold black marker hatching) from Window > Graphic Style Libraries > Scribble Effects (by script: open the library document and GraphicStyle.applyTo the item there, then duplicate it into the target).

cards.name: Isometric flat faces (scale, shear, rotate)
cards.summary: Flat front-view art (a facade, a screen, a label) is projected onto the left, right or top face of an isometric cube by the scale-shear-rotate method and stays fully editable vector.
use_for: isometric city, office and device illustrations
putting a logo or UI screen onto the side of an isometric box
avoid: true perspective with converging lines: use the Perspective Grid in Illustrator or Add Perspective in CorelDRAW
art that also needs side faces: extrude it (see the extruded 3D block recipe)
type you still need to edit a lot: it stays live but sheared type is awkward to edit; set the copy first

steps.note: Object > Transform > Scale, Non-Uniform: Horizontal 100 %, Vertical 86.602 %. DOM: item.resize(100, 86.602).

Object > Transform > Shear, Horizontal axis: -30 deg for the left face, +30 deg for the right face and the top face. DOM: m = app.getIdentityMatrix(); m.mValueC = Math.tan(a * Math.PI / 180); item.transform(m) (unverified).
Object > Transform > Rotate: -30 deg for the left face and the top face, +30 deg for the right face (positive = counter-clockwise). DOM: item.rotate(a).

steps.script:
a = 3.2
for k in ("orange_box", "zigzag"):
    labels[k].Delete()
def face(name, color, art, w, h, x):
    tile = layer.CreateRectangle2(x, 4.0, a, a, 0, 0, 0, 0)
    tile.Fill.ApplyUniformFill(rgb(color))
    tile.Outline.SetNoOutline()
    art.SetSize(w, h)
    art.CenterX = x + a / 2
    art.CenterY = 4.0 + a / 2
    art.OrderToFront()
    sr = app.CreateShapeRange()
    sr.Add(tile)
    sr.Add(art)
    labels[name] = sr.Group()
face("left", "#FF7A1A", labels["blue_star"], 2.0, 1.9, 1.5)
face("right", "#D9621A", labels["pgd_type"], 2.4, 0.8, 6.2)
face("top", "#FFC48A", labels["grad_circle"], 2.0, 2.0, 11.0)
result = labels["left"]
steps.note: Setup (script): deletes the box and the zigzag and builds three flat 3.2 in faces, each a coloured square grouped with plate art (star, type, circle).

steps.script:
import math
a = 3.2
w = a * math.cos(math.radians(30))
for name, sk, rot in (("left", 30, -30), ("right", -30, 30), ("top", 30, 30)):
    g = labels[name]
    g.Stretch(1.0, 0.86602)
    g.Skew(sk, 0)
    g.Rotate(rot)
X0, Y0 = PW / 2, 1.9
labels["left"].RightX = X0
labels["left"].BottomY = Y0
labels["right"].LeftX = X0
labels["right"].BottomY = Y0
labels["top"].CenterX = X0
labels["top"].BottomY = Y0 + a
result = labels["top"]
steps.note: Scale vertical 86.602 percent (Shape.Stretch), horizontal skew (Shape.Skew) and rotation (Shape.Rotate) per face: skew 30 / rotate -30 gives the left face, skew -30 / rotate 30 the right face, skew 30 / rotate 30 the top face (signs found with a probe run); the three faces are then moved so their edges meet in a cube.
script ran

verified.note: Three flat faces (star, PGD type, gradient circle) are sheared, scaled and rotated into the left, right and top faces of an isometric cube that meet cleanly; the circle becomes a correct top-face ellipse and the type runs along the right face.

manual_steps: Test the shear / skew sign on one square first (the angles above are the Illustrator dialog convention: left face shear -30 / rotate -30, right face +30 / +30, top face +30 / -30), then snap the three faces together along an isometric grid.

cards.name: Extruded 3D block
cards.summary: Flat icons, shapes and type are pushed back into solid 3D blocks with shaded side faces: a lit 3D render in Illustrator, editable flat-shaded vector faces in CorelDRAW.
avoid: Illustrator 3D and Materials when the file must stay clean vector (screen print, vinyl): it expands to an image; use CorelDRAW Extrude, or Illustrator's Extrude & Bevel (Classic) by hand
small text with a deep extrusion: the faces collide; lower the depth
photoreal materials in CorelDRAW: its faces are flat or two-colour shaded vectors

steps.note: The verified demo values (depth 150 pt, an off-axis view); send the other harvested keys at their defaults as the verified call did. A true isometric view is X -0.6155, Y +/-0.7854, Z 0 radians with FOV 0 (geometry, not render-tested); the panel's isometric rotation presets are the by-hand route.
Only when the file must not carry a live 3D effect: the result becomes an image (see avoid).

Extrude on the blue star: Back Parallel keeps the walls parallel (no taper). With a page-locked vanishing point (VPType 1) the walls run from the shape centre to that point, here 0.9 in right and 0.6 in down; colour shading from a mid blue to navy.

manual_steps: Ready-made looks: the '3D Effect 1' graphic style (Illustrator, Graphic Style Libraries > 3D Effects) or the 'Extrude1' preset on the CorelDRAW Extrude tool's property bar (no script call applies a .pst preset).

cards.name: Stepped blend and blend along a path
cards.summary: Two or more shapes are morphed in a set number of in-between steps: stepped colour ramps, shape tweens, tube and ribbon looks, or a row of objects that follows a curved spine.
use_for: stepped retro colour bands and sunbursts
neon tube / ribbon looks with many steps
repeating objects along a curved path
avoid: a smooth colour change inside one shape: a gradient is lighter
key objects with very different node structure: the steps twist; match the start points first
very high step counts on complex art: heavy, slow files

steps.note: Object > Blend > Blend Options: Spacing = Specified Steps (for example 12), Orientation = Align to Page (Align to Path when the steps should turn along a curved spine). Dialog only: no object-model setter.
With the key objects selected (pageItem.selected = true): app.executeMenuCommand('Path Blend Make') (confirmed by the harvest).
Optional, blend along a path: select the blend and a drawn path together, then Replace Spine (id paired from the shortcut list, not confirmed by running it).
Optional: bake the steps into plain paths (one-way).

steps.script:
import math
for k in ("grad_circle", "pgd_type"):
    labels[k].Delete()
sh = labels["blue_star"]
sh.ConvertToCurves()
c = sh.Curve
star = [(c.Nodes.Item(i).PositionX, c.Nodes.Item(i).PositionY) for i in range(1, c.Nodes.Count + 1)]
cx = sum(q[0] for q in star) / len(star)
cy = sum(q[1] for q in star) / len(star)
f = 2.3 / sh.SizeWidth
S = 1.9

def hit(poly, th):
    dx, dy = math.cos(th), math.sin(th)
    best = None
    for i in range(len(poly)):
        (x1, y1), (x2, y2) = poly[i], poly[(i + 1) % len(poly)]
        ex, ey = x2 - x1, y2 - y1
        den = dx * ey - dy * ex
        if abs(den) < 1e-12:
            continue
        t = ((x1 - cx) * ey - (y1 - cy) * ex) / den
        u = ((x1 - cx) * dy - (y1 - cy) * dx) / den
        if t > 0 and -1e-9 <= u <= 1 + 1e-9 and (best is None or t < best):
            best = t
    return (cx + best * dx, cy + best * dy)

box = [(cx - S / 2 / f, cy + S / 2 / f), (cx + S / 2 / f, cy + S / 2 / f), (cx + S / 2 / f, cy - S / 2 / f), (cx - S / 2 / f, cy - S / 2 / f)]
angs = [math.atan2(y - cy, x - cx) for x, y in star] + [math.atan2(y - cy, x - cx) for x, y in box]
angs = sorted(set(round(a, 6) for a in angs), key=lambda a: (math.pi / 2 - a) % (2 * math.pi))
print("nodes per shape:", len(angs))

def build(poly, ox, oy, rgbhex):
    pts = [hit(poly, a) for a in angs]
    pts = [(ox + (x - cx) * f, oy + (y - cy) * f) for x, y in pts]
    crv = app.CreateCurve(doc)
    sp = crv.CreateSubPath(pts[0][0], pts[0][1])
    for x, y in pts[1:]:
        sp.AppendLineSegment(x, y)
    sp.Closed = True
    shp = layer.CreateCurve(crv)
    shp.Fill.ApplyUniformFill(rgb(rgbhex))
    shp.Outline.SetNoOutline()
    return shp

labels["bstart"] = build(box, 3.0, 6.4, "#FF7A1A")
labels["bend"] = build(star, 17.0, 6.4, "#1E5BFF")
labels["orange_box"].Delete()
sh.Delete()
result = labels["bstart"]
steps.note: Setup (script): deletes the circle and the type, and rebuilds the box and the star as two 14-node closed polygons, both clockwise from the top and with a node at the same angle round the centre (the star's 10 corners plus 4 extra collinear nodes on its edges; the box's 4 corners plus 10 extra collinear nodes on its sides), so node k of the box maps to node k of the star and the blend cannot twist. The box is a plain 1.9 in square at the left (orange), the star 2.3 in wide at the right (blue).

steps.script:
blend = labels["bstart"].CreateBlend(labels["bend"], 12, 0, 0, 0.0, 0.0, False, None, False, 0, 0, False)
result = labels["bstart"]
steps.note: Blend from the box to the star in 12 steps (Shape.CreateBlend: the square is the start, the star the end): a shape and colour tween from orange to blue. Both ends have 14 matched nodes (see the setup step), so each in-between is a clean in-between shape, not a twist.

steps.script:
a = layer.CreateEllipse2(1.4, 1.6, 0.3)
b = layer.CreateEllipse2(18.6, 1.6, 0.3)
a.Fill.ApplyUniformFill(rgb("#E0006E"))
b.Fill.ApplyUniformFill(rgb("#FFD400"))
a.Outline.SetNoOutline()
b.Outline.SetNoOutline()
labels["zigzag"].Outline.SetNoOutline()
a.CreateBlend(b, 30, 0, 0, 0.0, 0.0, False, labels["zigzag"], True, 0, 0, False)
result = a

cards.name: Contour rings / topographic lines
cards.summary: Evenly spaced concentric outlines run inside or around a shape, for topographic map rings, retro multi-line lettering and op-art backgrounds.
use_for: retro multi-outline headlines (outline the type first)
avoid: inside contours with many steps on thin shapes: they run out of room and stop early; use fewer steps or To Center
a soft glow: use a blurred glow effect
bitmaps: vector objects only

steps.script:
for k in ("orange_box", "grad_circle", "pgd_type", "zigzag"):

star.Fill.ApplyNoFill()
star.Outline.Width = 0.03
star.Outline.Color.CopyAssign(rgb("#1B4F72"))
result = star

Contour on the star: 8 steps, 0.08 in apart, round corners, outline colour dark blue.

cards.name: Seamless pattern tile and grid repeat
cards.summary: A motif becomes a seamless repeating pattern swatch or a live grid of copies, for backgrounds, packaging fills and textile-style repeats.
use_for: quick dot or texture fills from the shipped libraries
avoid: photo textures: build raster repeats in Photoshop
unattended scripts: Illustrator's Make Pattern enters Pattern Editing Mode with an alert, CorelDRAW's Pattern Fill opens a capture dialog
tiles nobody checked at the edges: inspect the seams after applying the fill

steps.note: With the motif selected: creates a pattern swatch and enters Pattern Editing Mode; set Tile Type (Grid, Brick by Row, Hex), size and spacing in Pattern Options, then Done (by hand).

steps.script:
for k in ("orange_box", "grad_circle", "pgd_type", "zigzag"):
    labels[k].Delete()
bg = layer.CreateRectangle2(0.0, 0.0, PW, PH, 0, 0, 0, 0)
bg.Fill.ApplyUniformFill(rgb("#F6E7C8"))
bg.Outline.SetNoOutline()
bg.OrderToBack()
star = labels["blue_star"]
star.SetSize(1.1, 1.05)
star.LeftX, star.BottomY = 0.7, 9.4
dot = layer.CreateEllipse2(1.25 + 1.1, 8.3, 0.4)
dot.Fill.ApplyUniformFill(rgb("#FF7A1A"))
dot.Outline.SetNoOutline()
tile = app.CreateShapeRange()
tile.Add(star)
tile.Add(dot)
unit = tile.Group()
row = unit.StepAndRepeat(7, 2.5, 0.0)
rr = app.CreateShapeRange()
rr.Add(unit)
rr.AddRange(row)
band = rr.Group()
band.StepAndRepeat(3, 0.0, -2.6)
result = band

cards.name: Radial and mirror repeat (mandala, rosette)
cards.summary: One petal, spoke or half-drawing is repeated around a centre or mirrored across an axis, for mandalas, rosettes, sunbursts and symmetric emblems.
avoid: type running around a circle: use type on a path
copies that each need different content: duplicate and rotate them as separate objects
a cutting file: weld or expand the copies first

steps.note: 11 copies x 30 deg = a 12-fold ring pivoting on the art's centre: group the petal with an unpainted circle centred on the ring centre so the group centre is the pivot. Degrees and radians are stored twice: set both. Verified render: 4 copies, 15 deg, 80 % scale.
Optional: bake the ring into paths.

steps.script:
for k in list(labels):
    labels[k].Delete()
labels.clear()
cx, cy = PW / 2, PH / 2
colors = ["#FF7A1A", "#E0006E", "#1E5BFF"]
for i in range(12):
    petal = layer.CreateEllipse2(cx, cy + 2.1, 0.55, 1.6)
    petal.Fill.ApplyUniformFill(rgb(colors[i % 3]))
    petal.Outline.SetNoOutline()

hub = layer.CreateEllipse2(cx, cy, 0.7)
hub.Fill.ApplyUniformFill(rgb("#FFD400"))
hub.Outline.Width = 0.04
hub.Outline.Color.CopyAssign(rgb("#1A1A1A"))
result = hub
steps.note: Radial repeat (script): one petal ellipse is drawn above a centre point and repeated 12 times, each copy rotated 30 degrees more about the centre (Shape.RotateEx), in three alternating colours, with a hub on top. The plate shapes are deleted first.

cards.name: Warped / enveloped headline
cards.summary: A headline, logo word or badge text is bent into an arc, flag, bulge or custom outline while the text stays editable.
use_for: fitting a word into a shield or circle shape
sign text seen at an angle
avoid: text that must run along a circle with upright letters: use type on a path (Fit Text to Path in CorelDRAW)
strong bends on small text: illegible
wide art near the artboard edge: the warp grows the bounding box

steps.note: On the live type object or group; the text stays editable. DeformStyle switches the shape (3 Arc Upper, 4 Arch, 5 Bulge, 8 Flag, 9 Wave). Verified: Arc and Flag at 0.12, Wave at 1.0.

steps.script:
e = s.CreateEnvelope(1, 2, False)
c = e.Envelope.Container
l, r, b, tp = s.LeftX, s.RightX, s.BottomY, s.TopY
w = r - l
top = c.Segments.Item(2)
top.Type = 1
top.SetStartingControlPointPosition(l + w * 0.3, tp + 1.3)
top.SetEndingControlPointPosition(r - w * 0.3, tp + 1.3)
bot = c.Segments.Item(4)
bot.Type = 1
bot.SetStartingControlPointPosition(r - w * 0.3, b - 1.3)
bot.SetEndingControlPointPosition(l + w * 0.3, b - 1.3)
s.Outline.Width = 0.04
s.Outline.Color.CopyAssign(rgb("#1A1A1A"))
result = s

cards.name: Line-art icon (uniform stroke, rounded)
cards.summary: Icons drawn as single-weight outlines with round caps, round joins and softened corners, then strokes outlined and merged into a clean, scalable icon file.
use_for: consistent stroke icons for web and app
avoid: mixed stroke weights inside one set: pick one weight per icon size
outlining strokes too early: the weight can no longer change; keep a live master
tapered, inked lines: use a width profile instead of a uniform stroke

steps.note: Softens every corner (radius in pt, about the stroke weight). Set the stroke first in the DOM: pathItem.strokeWidth = 4; strokeCap = StrokeCap.ROUNDENDCAP; strokeJoin = StrokeJoin.ROUNDENDJOIN; filled = false. Verified at radius 45 pt.
Bake the rounded corners into the paths.
Object > Path > Outline Stroke: each stroke becomes a filled shape of the same width (confirmed id).
Group the outlined pieces so the next effect has a group.
Fuses touching same-colour pieces into one shape per colour. It must sit first in the group's appearance stack to act like the Pathfinder panel (the gallery's chain_first lesson).
Bake the merge into final paths.

steps.script:
for k in ("orange_box", "grad_circle", "pgd_type", "zigzag"):
    labels[k].Delete()
star = labels["blue_star"]
star.SetSize(4.4, 4.18)
star.CenterX, star.CenterY = PW / 2, PH / 2 - 0.1
ring = layer.CreateEllipse2(PW / 2, PH / 2, 2.3)
labels["ring"] = ring
for sh in (star, ring):
    sh.Fill.ApplyNoFill()
    sh.Outline.Width = 0.14
    sh.Outline.Color.CopyAssign(rgb("#1A1A1A"))
    sh.Outline.LineCaps = 1
    sh.Outline.LineJoin = 1
result = star
steps.note: Setup (script): deletes the other shapes; the star is scaled up and a ring is drawn round it so the two touch. Both get no fill and a 0.14 in dark outline with round caps and round joins (Outline.Width, LineCaps 1, LineJoin 1).
Fillet rounds each cusp corner of the star's outline path (Shape.Fillet, radius 0.12 in).

steps.script:
bodies = [layer.Shapes.Item(i) for i in range(1, layer.Shapes.Count + 1)]
objs = [sh.Outline.ConvertToObject() for sh in bodies]
icon = objs[0]
for o in objs[1:]:
    icon = o.Weld(icon)
icon.Fill.ApplyUniformFill(rgb("#1A1A1A"))
icon.Outline.SetNoOutline()
result = icon

cards.name: Flat icon with long shadow
cards.summary: A flat icon casts a hard-edged diagonal shadow that runs out to the edge of its background tile, the classic flat-design long shadow.
avoid: soft, realistic shadows: use a drop shadow
busy or photographic backgrounds: the hard shadow shape fights them
very complex outlines: the sweep gets heavy; simplify the silhouette first

steps.note: On a duplicate of the icon placed behind it: 150 copies, each 1 pt further along the diagonal. The vertical sign convention is not confirmed: if the copies climb up, use moveV_Pts -1.
Bake the copies into a group of paths.
The copies share one flat colour, so Merge fuses them into one shadow shape; it must sit first in the group's appearance stack (chain_first lesson).
Bake the merged shadow.
Shadow colour: a darker shade of the tile, or black at 20-30 % opacity in Multiply (pageItem.blendingMode = BlendModes.MULTIPLY).
Put a copy of the background tile on top, select it with the shadow, Make Clipping Mask so the shadow stops at the tile edge.

steps.script:
for k in ("orange_box", "grad_circle", "pgd_type", "zigzag"):
    labels[k].Delete()
    del labels[k]
tile = layer.CreateRectangle2(PW / 2 - 3.2, PH / 2 - 3.2, 6.4, 6.4, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, 0.5)
tile.Fill.ApplyUniformFill(rgb("#F6E7C8"))
tile.Outline.SetNoOutline()
tile.Name = "tile"
tile.OrderToBack()
icon = labels["blue_star"]
icon.SetSize(3.2, 3.04)
icon.CenterX = PW / 2
icon.CenterY = PH / 2
labels["tile"] = tile
labels["icon"] = icon
result = icon

Extrude on the icon: Back Parallel, one solid side colour, run 7 in right and 7 in down (45 degrees, page-locked vanishing point) so the walls pass the edge of the tile.

cards.name: Starburst, scallop and zigzag badge edges
cards.summary: Circles and polygons get sawtooth starburst spikes (or, as variants, scalloped seal edges and puffy petals) for badges, price stickers and decorative frames.
use_for: zigzag decorative borders and divider lines
avoid: detailed logos or body text: every segment gets teeth
too few anchors: a 4-point circle gives only a few lobes; add anchor points or start from a polygon
die-cut lines: uneven segments give uneven teeth; check the nodes

steps.note: Run it twice on a circle (4 -> 16 anchors) so the edge gets an even ridge rhythm (confirmed id).
Corner points give the sawtooth starburst; roundness 1 gives a scalloped wave (variant, not in the render test). Ridges are per segment. Verified at 18 pt, 5 ridges, corner points.
Zipper distortion on the gradient circle (CreateZipperDistortion at the circle's centre, amplitude 20, frequency 10, Random and Smooth off): sawtooth starburst spikes around the circle.
Convert to Curves bakes the teeth into nodes.
CreateZipperDistortion(15.625, 6.354165354330709, 20, 10, False, False, False)
InvokeItem(68000526-6be1-4205-b2e9-6c9dff00f4c5)

verified.note: The gradient circle gets an even ring of sawtooth teeth, a starburst price-badge edge. The layer list still shows the circle as an ellipse with a live distortion, so the Convert to Curves step does not appear to have baked it.

manual_steps: Puffy petal or spiky star variants: Illustrator Pucker & Bloat (d_factor -60 spikes was verified; +20 to +80 bloats into petals) or CorelDRAW Distort Push & Pull (Amplitude 60 gave needle spikes).
